transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:30 PST / 22:30 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Ava Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz (Nebula Analytics - Head of ML), Marco Ruiz (Nebula - CTO), Priya Singh (Nebula - SRE)

Summary: Quick discovery to understand Nebula's stack and interest in Redwood's PLG/self-serve API (quickstart, free credits, time-to-first-token), and to qualify production constraints (latency, data residency, SOC 2). Nebula is evaluating hosted first but has some regulated customers that may require VPC/private options later.

[00:00] Samir: Hey all thanks for making time, I'm Samir from Redwood, with Ava who's our solutions engineer. Quick intro, want to hear about your use case and constraints then demo the quickstart flow.
[00:28] Marco: Hi thanks, I'm Marco, CTO. We're Nebula Analytics, focus on real-time insights for finance clients. We have a PLG-ish funnel but most of the high-touch enterprise work needs stricter controls.
[00:46] Lena: Hi, I'm Lena, head of ML. We're currently using a mix of hosted APIs and self-hosted models depending on cost. Right now latency is a big thing for us on interactive features — aim for p95 < 200ms for the 1k token-ish prompts. Costs are also significant, looking to drop per-token unit cost.
[01:10] Ava: Got it. Quick question on stack: are you hosting models yourselves or using external APIs? Any preferred cloud or region?
[01:20] Priya: We use GCP primarily, some customers in EU need data residency. For now we mostly call OpenAI endpoints for prototyping, but we run a few local quantized models for internal experiments.
[01:34] Samir: That makes sense. Typical mix. The quickstart we usually recommend gets you to a first token in <10 minutes — sign up, create an API key, run the quickstart notebook or a cURL request, and you'll see a sample response. We also give free credits for trials so you can run a few thousand tokens and pilot.
[01:58] Marco: How quick is the SDK? Can my team plug in and see real latency numbers quickly?
[02:06] Ava: Yes, the SDK ships with a metrics endpoint and a local profiler you can enable. For the hosted API you'll get token-level timing in the console and SDK telemetry so you'll know p50/p95. For dedicated we can provide baseline throughput numbers per GPU type.
[02:28] Lena: On the security side, we need SOC 2 and KMS integration, SSO. What's Redwood's posture?
[02:36] Samir: Redwood is SOC 2 certified, we support SAML SSO and RBAC. For key management we integrate with customer KMS options on Dedicated/Private. Hosted supports envelope encryption and bring-your-own-key via KMS for enterprise tiers. We'll share the security docs.
[02:58] Priya: Good. Also curious about Private — if we need VPC or on-prem later, is migration straightforward?
[03:06] Ava: Yes, we maintain a consistent API and config layer across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Migration is mostly switching endpoints and, for Private, a brief onboarding to attach your network and KMS. The runtime and model variants behave similarly so minimal app changes.
[03:28] Marco: How do you handle fallbacks when capacity is constrained? We worry about graceful degradation for customer-facing features.
[03:35] Samir: We do smart routing and model variant fallback — you can policy route by latency or cost, and set automatic fallbacks to a quantized variant or lower tier when capacity is low. That keeps apps online with graceful quality degradation.
[03:55] Lena: Performance question: we've seen big gaps using non-optimized kernels for some transformer variants. Do you provide kernel selection and quantization profiles?
[04:03] Ava: Yup — our runtime selects kernels based on model arch and sequence length distribution. We also provide recommended quantization profiles per model and guidance on perf vs. quality tradeoffs. For example, for 2k seqs we recommend X quantization on A100 or Bf16 kernels on newer hardware.
[04:28] Marco: For the PLG quickstart, what's the friction for product engineers? We want a low time-to-first-token to show value quickly.
[04:36] Samir: The flow is a 3-step: sign up, get free credits, run quickstart notebook. Typical devs hit a first token in under 10 minutes. We provide sample prompt sets and prebuilt SDK snippets for Python, Node, and curl. We'll share a quickstart link and sample app repo.
[04:58] Priya: Any limits on the trial org? Rate limits or limited model catalog?
[05:04] Ava: Trial orgs have rate limits but they're generous for evaluation. You get access to a curated set of open models and a couple of Redwood-verified variants. If you need a specific model we can enable it for the trial.
[05:20] Marco: Cost question — for production, is Dedicated always cheaper per-token vs Hosted? We need numbers to justify a reserved commit.
[05:28] Samir: It depends on utilization. Dedicated with reserved capacity typically reduces unit cost when utilization is high (sustained throughput). Hosted is better for bursty workloads and fastest time-to-value. We'll send a pricing compare sheet with example unit economics for different throughput profiles.
[05:50] Lena: Also interested in batching and caching — our workload has many similar prefixes.
[05:56] Ava: Auto prefix/KV caching and workload-aware batching are built into the runtime and can be enabled per-route. That yields big cost wins for chat/history-like workloads. We can run a caching benchmark during the POC.
[06:15] Marco: Ok, sounds good. For the POC we want to run 1k sample prompts and measure latency/cost across hosted vs dedicated (small cluster) and see quality delta across quantized models.
[06:25] Samir: Perfect. Action items — we'll provision a trial org with free credits, Ava will share the quickstart notebook and sample prompt set. You (Priya) will send us the 1k sample queries, and we'll schedule a technical deep dive next week to start the benchmark.

[06:48] -- short demo walkthrough (screen share) --
[07:02] Ava: (screen) Signing up is email, add org name, create API key. Here's the quickstart notebook: import redwood, set API_KEY, run client.chat.create. I'll paste the sample curl — note the streaming option for lower latency perceived by users.
[07:28] Marco: I see the console shows token breakdown and latency metrics per route — that's really useful. Is there an API to pull those metrics to our internal dashboards?
[07:37] Ava: Yes, the metrics API and webhooks let you export token-level cost and latency; can push to Datadog/Grafana. We also have a tracing hook for request-level correlation.
[07:58] Lena: Regarding SSO and RBAC, can we map roles to projects and restrict model variants for certain users?
[08:06] Samir: Yes, RBAC supports project-level permissions and you can restrict which models or over-ride config per project.
[08:20] Priya: A small nit: for EU data residency, will hosted support an EU region with data residency guarantee?
[08:27] Samir: Hosted supports EU regions, and for enterprise we offer data residency controls; for strict residency customers we recommend Dedicated or Private with region pinning. We'll include the residency SLA notes in the security doc.
[08:48] Marco: Any known limitations on model sizes or sequence lengths for streaming?
[08:54] Ava: Streaming works fine up to large seqs, but throughput and latency depend on model size and hardware. For very long contexts we recommend KV caching and careful batching. We'll share best practices.

[09:20] -- wrap up and recap --
[09:30] Samir: Recap: we'll provision trial, share quickstart + SDK + security docs, Nebula will send sample prompts, schedule technical deep dive/benchmark for Tue 2026-03-10. I'll send pricing comparison.
[09:48] Marco: Great, look forward to it.
[09:52] Lena: Thanks everyone.
[09:55] Meeting end.
